affiliations.date_precision: The JSOU monograph calls Gordon Browne a former Boston insurance executive when describing his spring 1942 COI/OSS work. It supplies no company, exact employment dates, or proof that this was his immediate predecessor role.
affiliations.research_notes: The distinctive indexed name, official CIA description of Gordon Browne on the original Tangier COI team, and JSOU's matching Tangier account support a high-confidence identity. The indexed middle initial and private identifier still require Box 87 confirmation. No insurance company is inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Warren G. Brown is confirmed as the Army entrant represented by the exact-name and private-identifier match in the official merged file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The full name and private service identifier match across the OSS index and official Army-entry file; the identifier is withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private identifier and exact full indexed name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army-entry record is dated April 7, 1942; the index documents an OSS personnel file but not the OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The Army entry records private rank PVT. Its residual occupation code 999 is not converted into an occupation, employer, industry, or immediate predecessor role.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Willis K. Brown row conflicts with the official Army record tied to the same private identifier, which gives the first name as Willie.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Army bulk file links the index's private identifier to Willie K. Brown rather than Willis K. Brown; the identifier and unrelated record details are withheld.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Conflicting. A unique private identifier is strong evidence, but the given-name difference cannot be treated as a silent spelling correction.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record predates the indexed OSS file, but the identity conflict prevents use of its chronology or occupation for this profile.
claims.match_notes: The conflict is preserved for archival review. The Army record's rank, date, birthplace, and occupation are not assigned to the indexed person.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Gordon H. Browne is a high-confidence match to the Gordon Browne documented on the original COI/OSS team in Tangier.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Original COI team for TORCH consisted of
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official CIA material names Gordon Browne on the original Tangier COI team; a JSOU monograph independently gives the same name, place, operational context, and prior occupation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive exact surname and given name in two authoritative OSS accounts matching the indexed Gordon H. Browne; the sources omit the middle initial and private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Both accounts place Gordon Browne with the Tangier COI/OSS team in spring 1942; the index does not provide an appointment date.
claims.match_notes: The match is visibly qualified pending Box 87 confirmation. The official Army merged file's failure to return the index's officer-style identifier is not disproof because that dataset has documented omissions.

research_attempts.query_text: Willis K. Brown: visually checked NARA index; exact private-identifier Army bulk and technical-documentation review; Willis and Willie name variants; exact-name OSS, CIA, employer, occupation, institutional, newspaper, obituary, directory, military, and archival searches; OSS Operational Groups roster.
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: The exact private identifier resolves to Willie K. Brown rather than the index's Willis K. Brown. The difference is not silently normalized, and common-name candidates without the identifier or Box 87 linkage were rejected.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually checked index supplies the distinctive name Gordon H. Browne, a private officer-style identifier, and Box 87.
